subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the maximum percentage rectification in half wave and full wave rectifiers?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. TRANSCRIPTION: the book prints 'perecentage' twice; the word is spelled correctly here. Physics hand-checked: the standard maxima are 4/π² = 0.406 and 8/π² = 0.812, so 40.6% and 81.2% — the full wave figure is exactly twice the half wave figure.

recall_prompt: Give the two maximum efficiency figures — half wave first, then full wave.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Half wave rectifier
lines: in a half wave rectifier is 40.6%.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The figure with the per cent sign.
steps.why: A half wave rectifier throws away one half of every cycle, so at best it can deliver only about two fifths of the input power as d.c. The exact maximum is 4/π² = 0.406.
common_mistakes: Writing 50%. Half the cycle is used, but that does not make the efficiency 50%.
Leaving out the per cent sign. The question asks for a percentage.

recall.must_convey: That the maximum efficiency of a half wave rectifier is 40.6%.
reject: eighty one point two per cent

steps.memory_tip: Half wave 40.6, full wave exactly double: 81.2.

steps.label: Full wave rectifier
lines: in a full wave rectifier is 81.2%.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Exactly twice the half wave figure.
steps.why: A full wave rectifier uses both halves of every cycle, so it delivers twice the d.c. power for the same input. The exact maximum is 8/π² = 0.812, which is why the two figures are in the ratio 2 : 1.
common_mistakes: Writing 100%. Even a full wave rectifier cannot reach 100%.
Swapping the two figures. The larger number belongs to the full wave rectifier.

recall.must_convey: That the maximum efficiency of a full wave rectifier is 81.2%.
accept: eighty one point two per cent

steps.memory_tip: Both halves used, so double the efficiency: 2 × 40.6 = 81.2.

insider_note: Two numbers, one mark each. If only one is remembered, the other is its double or its half — 40.6 and 81.2.
